subject: Film & Cinema
title: Voiceover: Help or Crutch?
description: A fast breakdown of Voiceover: Help or Crutch? for builders.

hook.text: Goodfellas uses voiceover brilliantly. Lesser films use it to explain what they can't show.

buildup.text: Voiceover can add intimacy, irony, or unreliable narration to a screenplay.

discovery.text: It works when it adds a layer the images can't provide — tone, memory, lies.

twist.text: Screenwriting teachers often call voiceover lazy because it 'tells' instead of 'shows.'

climax.text: The real rule: voiceover should never duplicate what's already on screen.

punchline.text: If the picture tells the story, stay quiet.

quiz.question: When does voiceover work well in a screenplay?
options: When it adds a layer the images alone can't provide
